text:
Predicates:
Schedule(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in the company on day y.
Lunch(x, y) ::: x has lunch in place y.
Work(x, y) ::: x works remotely from place y.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InCountry(x, y) ::: x is in country y.
Premises:
∀x (Schedule(x, customers) → Appear(x, today)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (Lunch(x, company) → Schedule(x, customers)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
Lunch(x, company) ⊕ Lunch(x, home) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
Lunch(x, home) → Work(x, home) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InCountry(x, otherCountries) → Work(x, home)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬Work(x, home)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james, today)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ Appear(james, today)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
Lunch(james, company) ::: James has lunch in the company.
